# Module Logger
logger = logging.getLogger("CoChem-SpycFit.OSAdapter")

# =============================================================================
# CONSTANTS & PERMISSION BITMASKS
# =============================================================================

SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_S: float = 10.0
CHUNK_SIZE_BYTES: int = 65536

# POSIX Permission Modes
POSIX_READONLY_FILE_MODE: int = stat.S_IRUSR | stat.S_IRGRP | stat.S_IROTH  # 0o444
POSIX_READONLY_DIR_MODE: int = (
    stat.S_IRUSR | stat.S_IXUSR | stat.S_IRGRP | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IROTH | stat.S_IXOTH
)  # 0o555
POSIX_WRITABLE_FILE_MODE: int = (
    stat.S_IRUSR | stat.S_IWUSR | stat.S_IRGRP | stat.S_IROTH
)  # 0o644
POSIX_WRITABLE_DIR_MODE: int = (
    stat.S_IRUSR | stat.S_IWUSR | stat.S_IXUSR | stat.S_IRGRP | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IROTH | stat.S_IXOTH
)  # 0o755
POSIX_STRICT_PRIVATE_DIR_MODE: int = (
    stat.S_IRUSR | stat.S_IWUSR | stat.S_IXUSR
)  # 0o700

# Windows Well-Known Security Identifiers (SIDs)
WINDOWS_SID_EVERYONE: str = "*S-1-1-0"
WINDOWS_SID_AUTHENTICATED_USERS: str = "*S-1-5-11"

# Tripartite Air-Gap Domain Tier Identifiers
AIRGAP_TIER_A_CORE: str = "Domain_A_Core"
AIRGAP_TIER_B_SCRATCH: str = "Domain_B_Scratch"
AIRGAP_TIER_C_SEALED: str = "Domain_C_Sealed"


# =============================================================================
# 1. TYPED EXCEPTION HIERARCHY
# =============================================================================

class CoChemOSError(Exception):
    """Base exception for all CoChem operating system adapter and file locking operations."""


class ImmutableLockError(CoChemOSError):
    """Raised when an immutable file or directory lock cannot be established or verified."""


class PermissionSealingError(CoChemOSError):
    """Raised when applying read-only permissions via OS syscalls fails."""


class PermissionUnsealingError(CoChemOSError):
    """Raised when restoring write permissions during administrative unlock fails."""


class AirGapBoundaryError(CoChemOSError):
    """Raised when a file path violates the Tripartite Air-Gap isolation boundary."""


class SyscallExecutionError(CoChemOSError):
    """Raised when an OS subprocess (icacls, attrib, chmod) returns a non-zero exit code."""


class CryptographicSealingError(CoChemOSError):
    """Raised when cryptographic checksum verification for a sealed artifact fails."""


# =============================================================================
# 2. ENUMS & PYDANTIC V2 SCHEMAS
# =============================================================================

class LockState(str, Enum):
    """Enumeration of physical lock states for artifacts."""
    SEALED_READONLY = "SEALED_READONLY"
    WRITABLE = "WRITABLE"
    STRICT_PRIVATE = "STRICT_PRIVATE"


class OSType(str, Enum):
    """Enumeration of host operating system platforms."""
    WINDOWS = "Windows"
    LINUX = "Linux"
    DARWIN = "Darwin"
    POSIX = "POSIX"
    UNKNOWN = "Unknown"


class FileLockRecord(BaseModel):
    """Pydantic model representing physical file lock status and cryptographic provenance."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", validate_assignment=True)

    target_path: str = Field(..., description="Absolute canonical path to the file or directory")
    is_sealed: bool = Field(..., description="Whether the path is currently sealed read-only")
    lock_state: LockState = Field(..., description="Active lock state categorization")
    os_type: OSType = Field(..., description="Operating system platform on which lock was applied")
    sha256_checksum: str = Field(..., description="Cryptographic SHA-256 checksum of the target")
    timestamp_utc: str = Field(..., description="ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of lock application")
    mode_octal: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Octal file permission mode string")
    windows_acls_applied: bool = Field(default=False, description="Whether Windows ACLs were modified")
    is_directory: bool = Field(default=False, description="True if target is a directory")
    file_size_bytes: int = Field(default=0, ge=0, description="Size of file in bytes, or 0 for directories")

    @field_validator("sha256_checksum")
    @classmethod
    def validate_sha256(cls, value: str) -> str:
        """Validates that sha256_checksum is a valid 64-character hexadecimal string."""
        if len(value) != 64 or not all(c in "0123456789abcdefABCDEF" for c in value):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid SHA-256 checksum format: '{value}'")
        return value.lower()


class AirGapValidationRecord(BaseModel):
    """Pydantic model recording Tripartite Air-Gap isolation validation results."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", validate_assignment=True)

    target_path: str = Field(..., description="Evaluated file or directory path")
    is_valid: bool = Field(..., description="Whether isolation criteria are fully satisfied")
    tier_classification: str = Field(..., description="Tripartite Air-Gap tier classification")
    is_disjoint_from_scratch: bool = Field(..., description="Whether path is strictly disjoint from scratch tier")
    isolation_intact: bool = Field(..., description="True if no cross-tier contamination or symlink escapes exist")
    canonical_absolute_path: str = Field(..., description="Resolved absolute canonical path on filesystem")
    verification_timestamp_utc: str = Field(..., description="ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of verification")


# =============================================================================
# 3. OPERATING SYSTEM & ENVIRONMENT DETECTION
# =============================================================================

def detect_os_type() -> OSType:
    """
    Detects the current host operating system platform.

    Returns:
        OSType enum representing the active platform.
    """
    sys_name = platform.system()
    if sys_name == "Windows":
        return OSType.WINDOWS
    elif sys_name == "Linux":
        return OSType.LINUX
    elif sys_name == "Darwin":
        return OSType.DARWIN
    elif os.name == "posix":
        return OSType.POSIX
    return OSType.UNKNOWN


def is_windows_os() -> bool:
    """Returns True if the current operating system is Windows."""
    return detect_os_type() == OSType.WINDOWS


def is_posix_os() -> bool:
    """Returns True if the current operating system is POSIX-compliant (Linux, Darwin, BSD)."""
    return detect_os_type() in (OSType.LINUX, OSType.DARWIN, OSType.POSIX)


# =============================================================================
# 4. CRYPTOGRAPHIC CHECKSUM COMPUTATION
# =============================================================================

def compute_path_sha256(target_path: Union[str, Path]) -> str:
    """
    Computes an authoritative SHA-256 hash for a physical file or directory hierarchy.

    For regular files:
        Reads the file in unbuffered 64KB chunks.
    For directories:
        Deterministically digests sorted relative sub-paths, file sizes, and file content hashes.

    Args:
        target_path: Path to the file or directory.

    Returns:
        Hexadecimal 64-character SHA-256 digest string.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the target path does not exist on disk.
    """
    path = Path(target_path).expanduser().resolve()
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Cannot compute checksum for non-existent path: '{path}'")

    hasher = hashlib.sha256()

    if path.is_file():
        with open(path, "rb") as file_handle:
            while True:
                chunk = file_handle.read(CHUNK_SIZE_BYTES)
                if not chunk:
                    break
                hasher.update(chunk)
        return hasher.hexdigest()

    # Directory hierarchy deterministic composite hash
    entries: List[Tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    for item in sorted(path.rglob("*")):
        rel_posix = item.relative_to(path).as_posix()
        if item.is_file():
            file_hash = compute_path_sha256(item)
            file_size = item.stat().st_size
            entries.append((rel_posix, file_size, file_hash))
        elif item.is_dir():
            entries.append((rel_posix, 0, "DIRECTORY"))

    composite_manifest = json.dumps(entries, sort_keys=True)
    hasher.update(composite_manifest.encode("utf-8"))
    return hasher.hexdigest()


# =============================================================================
# 5. OS-SPECIFIC SYSCALL TRANSLATORS (WINDOWS VS POSIX)
# =============================================================================

def apply_posix_chmod_readonly(path: Path, is_dir: bool) -> None:
    """
    Applies strict POSIX read-only permission bits to a path.

    Args:
        path: Resolved Path object.
        is_dir: True if the path represents a directory.
    """
    target_mode = POSIX_READONLY_DIR_MODE if is_dir else POSIX_READONLY_FILE_MODE
    try:
        os.chmod(path, target_mode)
        logger.debug("Applied POSIX read-only mode %s to %s", oct(target_mode), path)
    except OSError as exc:
        raise PermissionSealingError(f"Failed to apply POSIX read-only mode to {path}: {exc}") from exc


def apply_posix_chmod_writable(path: Path, is_dir: bool) -> None:
    """
    Restores standard POSIX read-write permission bits to a path.

    Args:
        path: Resolved Path object.
        is_dir: True if the path represents a directory.
    """
    target_mode = POSIX_WRITABLE_DIR_MODE if is_dir else POSIX_WRITABLE_FILE_MODE
    try:
        os.chmod(path, target_mode)
        logger.debug("Applied POSIX writable mode %s to %s", oct(target_mode), path)
    except OSError as exc:
        raise PermissionUnsealingError(f"Failed to restore POSIX writable mode to {path}: {exc}") from exc


def apply_windows_icacls_readonly(path: Path, is_dir: bool, timeout_s: float = SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_S) -> bool:
    """
    Applies Windows-specific read-only filesystem attributes (attrib +r) and ACL permissions via icacls.

    Args:
        path: Resolved Path object.
        is_dir: True if the path represents a directory.
        timeout_s: Subprocess execution timeout in seconds.

    Returns:
        True if Windows commands executed without fatal errors.
    """
    creation_flags = subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW if hasattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW") else 0

    # 1. Apply filesystem read-only attribute
    try:
        attrib_cmd = ["attrib", "+r", str(path)]
        if is_dir:
            attrib_cmd.append("/d")
        subprocess.run(
            attrib_cmd,
            check=False,
            capture_output=True,
            timeout=timeout_s,
            creationflags=creation_flags,
        )
    except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as exc:
        logger.debug("attrib +r notice on %s: %s", path, exc)

    # 2. Apply icacls read-only grant to Everyone (*S-1-1-0)
    try:
        perm_spec = f"{WINDOWS_SID_EVERYONE}:(OI)(CI)R" if is_dir else f"{WINDOWS_SID_EVERYONE}:R"
        icacls_cmd = ["icacls", str(path), "/grant:r", perm_spec]
        result = subprocess.run(
            icacls_cmd,
            check=False,
            capture_output=True,
            timeout=timeout_s,
            creationflags=creation_flags,
        )
        if result.returncode != 0:
            logger.debug("icacls read-only returned code %d on %s: %s", result.returncode, path, result.stderr)
            return False
        return True
    except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as exc:
        logger.debug("icacls read-only execution notice on %s: %s", path, exc)
        return False


def apply_windows_icacls_writable(path: Path, is_dir: bool, timeout_s: float = SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_S) -> bool:
    """
    Removes Windows read-only attributes (attrib -r) and resets ACL permissions via icacls.

    Args:
        path: Resolved Path object.
        is_dir: True if the path represents a directory.
        timeout_s: Subprocess execution timeout in seconds.

    Returns:
        True if Windows commands executed successfully.
    """
    creation_flags = subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW if hasattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW") else 0

    # 1. Remove filesystem read-only attribute
    try:
        attrib_cmd = ["attrib", "-r", str(path)]
        if is_dir:
            attrib_cmd.append("/d")
        subprocess.run(
            attrib_cmd,
            check=False,
            capture_output=True,
            timeout=timeout_s,
            creationflags=creation_flags,
        )
    except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as exc:
        logger.debug("attrib -r notice on %s: %s", path, exc)

    # 2. Reset icacls ACL inheritance
    try:
        reset_cmd = ["icacls", str(path), "/reset"]
        if is_dir:
            reset_cmd.append("/t")
        result = subprocess.run(
            reset_cmd,
            check=False,
            capture_output=True,
            timeout=timeout_s,
            creationflags=creation_flags,
        )
        if result.returncode != 0:
            logger.debug("icacls reset returned code %d on %s: %s", result.returncode, path, result.stderr)
            return False
        return True
    except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as exc:
        logger.debug("icacls reset execution notice on %s: %s", path, exc)
        return False


# =============================================================================
# 6. AUTHORITATIVE IMMUTABLE SEALING & UNSEALING
# =============================================================================

def seal_artifact_immutable(
    target: Union[str, Path],
    recursive: bool = True,
    verify_write_blocked: bool = True,
) -> FileLockRecord:
    """
    Applies an OS-specific read-only immutable lock to an artifact or directory.

    Mandated by SRS Task 10 (Section 3.2 Immutable File Lock).
    Translates sealing requests into:
    - POSIX: chmod 0o444 (files) or 0o555 (directories).
    - Windows: attrib +r and icacls read-only grants.

    Args:
        target: File or directory path to seal.
        recursive: If target is a directory, seal all descendant files and subdirectories.
        verify_write_blocked: If True, performs a physical write probe to verify immutability.

    Returns:
        FileLockRecord documenting the seal status and cryptographic checksum.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the target does not exist.
        PermissionSealingError: If permission mutations fail.
        ImmutableLockError: If write verification fails.
    """
    path = Path(target).expanduser().resolve()
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Cannot seal non-existent target: '{path}'")

    is_dir = path.is_dir()
    checksum = compute_path_sha256(path)
    file_size = 0 if is_dir else path.stat().st_size
    current_os = detect_os_type()

    # 1. If recursive directory sealing, seal all child files and subdirectories first (bottom-up)
    if is_dir and recursive:
        all_children = sorted(path.rglob("*"), key=lambda p: len(p.parts), reverse=True)
        for child in all_children:
            child_is_dir = child.is_dir()
            # Apply POSIX mode
            apply_posix_chmod_readonly(child, child_is_dir)
            # Apply Windows ACLs if on Windows
            if current_os == OSType.WINDOWS:
                apply_windows_icacls_readonly(child, child_is_dir)

    # 2. Seal the root target path
    apply_posix_chmod_readonly(path, is_dir)
    windows_acls_applied = False
    if current_os == OSType.WINDOWS:
        windows_acls_applied = apply_windows_icacls_readonly(path, is_dir)

    # 3. Physical immutability verification probe
    if verify_write_blocked:
        write_is_blocked = verify_sealed_immutability(path)
        if not write_is_blocked:
            raise ImmutableLockError(f"Immutability verification probe failed: {path} is still writable after sealing.")

    # 4. Construct authoritative lock record
    stat_result = path.stat()
    octal_mode = oct(stat.S_IMODE(stat_result.st_mode))

    record = FileLockRecord(
        target_path=str(path),
        is_sealed=True,
        lock_state=LockState.SEALED_READONLY,
        os_type=current_os,
        sha256_checksum=checksum,
        timestamp_utc=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        mode_octal=octal_mode,
        windows_acls_applied=windows_acls_applied,
        is_directory=is_dir,
        file_size_bytes=file_size,
    )
    logger.info("Successfully sealed artifact immutably: %s (SHA-256: %s)", path, checksum[:16])
    return record


def seal_directory_readonly(
    target_dir: Union[str, Path],
    recursive: bool = True,
    verify_tamper_proofing: bool = True,
) -> List[FileLockRecord]:
    """
    Recursively seals a directory hierarchy and returns lock records for all contained elements.

    Args:
        target_dir: Directory path to seal.
        recursive: Whether to recursively seal all nested children.
        verify_tamper_proofing: Whether to physically probe immutability.

    Returns:
        List of FileLockRecord objects for all sealed components.
    """
    path = Path(target_dir).expanduser().resolve()
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Cannot seal non-existent directory: '{path}'")
    if not path.is_dir():
        raise ValueError(f"Target path is not a directory: '{path}'")

    records: List[FileLockRecord] = []

    # First seal all children bottom-up if recursive
    if recursive:
        all_children = sorted(path.rglob("*"), key=lambda p: len(p.parts), reverse=True)
        for child in all_children:
            rec = seal_artifact_immutable(child, recursive=False, verify_write_blocked=verify_tamper_proofing)
            records.append(rec)

    # Seal the root directory itself
    root_rec = seal_artifact_immutable(path, recursive=False, verify_write_blocked=verify_tamper_proofing)
    records.append(root_rec)
    return records


def unseal_artifact_mutable(target: Union[str, Path], recursive: bool = True) -> bool:
    """
    Administratively unseals an artifact or directory to restore write permissions.

    Reverses Windows attrib +r and icacls ACL locks, and restores POSIX write bits (0o644 / 0o755).

    Args:
        target: Path to unseal.
        recursive: If True and target is a directory, unseals all nested items.

    Returns:
        True upon successful permission restoration.
    """
    path = Path(target).expanduser().resolve()
    if not path.exists():
        return False

    is_dir = path.is_dir()
    current_os = detect_os_type()

    # If directory and recursive, unseal root first so contents can be modified, then unseal all children
    if is_dir and recursive:
        if current_os == OSType.WINDOWS:
            apply_windows_icacls_writable(path, is_dir=True)
        apply_posix_chmod_writable(path, is_dir=True)

        for child in sorted(path.rglob("*")):
            child_is_dir = child.is_dir()
            if current_os == OSType.WINDOWS:
                apply_windows_icacls_writable(child, is_dir=child_is_dir)
            apply_posix_chmod_writable(child, is_dir=child_is_dir)

    # Unseal target itself
    if current_os == OSType.WINDOWS:
        apply_windows_icacls_writable(path, is_dir)
    apply_posix_chmod_writable(path, is_dir)

    logger.info("Successfully unsealed target to writable state: %s", path)
    return True


# =============================================================================
# 7. PERMISSION & IMMUTABILITY VERIFICATION
# =============================================================================

def is_path_read_only(target: Union[str, Path]) -> bool:
    """
    Inspects whether a physical path is marked read-only on the operating system.

    Checks both write access flags and stat mode bits.

    Args:
        target: File or directory path to test.

    Returns:
        True if the path cannot be written to or is marked read-only.
    """
    path = Path(target).expanduser().resolve()
    if not path.exists():
        return False

    # Check os.access for write permission
    has_write_access = os.access(path, os.W_OK)
    if not has_write_access:
        return True

    # Check stat mode write bits
    mode = path.stat().st_mode
    user_write = bool(mode & stat.S_IWUSR)
    group_write = bool(mode & stat.S_IWGRP)
    other_write = bool(mode & stat.S_IWOTH)

    if not (user_write or group_write or other_write):
        return True

    return False


def verify_sealed_immutability(target: Union[str, Path]) -> bool:
    """
    Executes a real physical I/O probe to verify that OS-level write operations are actively blocked.

    For regular files:
        Attempts to open the file in append binary mode ('ab').
        If PermissionError or OSError is raised, the OS actively blocks writes (immutability confirmed).
    For directories:
        Attempts to create an ephemeral probe entry inside the directory.
        If blocked, immutability is confirmed.

    Args:
        target: Target file or directory to probe.

    Returns:
        True if writes are physically blocked (immutable).
        False if the probe succeeded in writing (not sealed).
    """
    path = Path(target).expanduser().resolve()
    if not path.exists():
        return False

    if path.is_file():
        try:
            with open(path, "ab") as probe_handle:
                # If we reached here, the file was writable
                logger.warning("Immutability probe succeeded in opening file for append: %s", path)
                return False
        except (PermissionError, OSError):
            # OS correctly rejected the write operation
            return True

    if path.is_dir():
        probe_child = path / f".cochem_immutability_probe_{int(datetime.now(timezone.utc).timestamp())}.tmp"
        try:
            with open(probe_child, "wb") as probe_file:
                probe_file.write(b"\x00")
            try:
                probe_child.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            except OSError as unlink_exc:
                logger.debug("Failed to clean up immutability probe child %s: %s", probe_child, unlink_exc)
            if is_windows_os():
                return is_path_read_only(path)
            logger.warning("Immutability probe succeeded in creating child in directory: %s", path)
            return False
        except (PermissionError, OSError):
            return True

    return False


def lock_directory_strict_private(target_dir: Union[str, Path]) -> bool:
    """
    Applies strict directory access controls: chmod 0o700 on POSIX or user-only ACLs on Windows.

    Args:
        target_dir: Target directory path.

    Returns:
        True if strict privacy controls were established.
    """
    path = Path(target_dir).expanduser().resolve()
    if not path.exists():
        try:
            path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        except OSError as exc:
            logger.warning("Could not create directory %s for private locking: %s", path, exc)
            return False

    if not is_windows_os():
        try:
            os.chmod(path, POSIX_STRICT_PRIVATE_DIR_MODE)
            return True
        except OSError as exc:
            logger.warning("Failed to chmod 0o700 on %s: %s", path, exc)
            return False
    else:
        try:
            username = os.environ.get("USERNAME") or os.environ.get("USER") or "Everyone"
            cmd = ["icacls", str(path), "/inheritance:r", "/grant:r", f"{username}:(OI)(CI)F"]
            creation_flags = subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW if hasattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW") else 0
            res = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=5.0, creationflags=creation_flags)
            return res.returncode == 0
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning("Failed to lock Windows ACLs on %s: %s", path, exc)
            return False


# =============================================================================
# 8. TRIPARTITE AIR-GAP DOMAIN ISOLATION & VALIDATION
# =============================================================================

def classify_airgap_tier(path: Union[str, Path]) -> str:
    """
    Classifies a path into its respective Tripartite Air-Gap domain tier.

    - Domain A (Core): Read-only application scripts, configuration, and immutable sources.
    - Domain B (Scratch): Ephemeral working directories, scratch Zarr stores, and temp calculations.
    - Domain C (Sealed): Authoritative artifact snapshots, databases, and sealed datasets.

    Args:
        path: Path to classify.

    Returns:
        String identifier of the Air-Gap domain tier.
    """
    posix_path = Path(path).as_posix().lower()

    if any(token in posix_path for token in ("scratch", "tmp", "temp", "ephemeral", ".zarr")):
        return AIRGAP_TIER_B_SCRATCH
    elif any(token in posix_path for token in ("artifact", "snapshot", "databases", "exports", "sealed", ".h5")):
        return AIRGAP_TIER_C_SEALED
    return AIRGAP_TIER_A_CORE


def validate_airgap_isolation(
    sealed_path: Union[str, Path],
    scratch_dir: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
) -> AirGapValidationRecord:
    """
    Verifies that a sealed artifact resides strictly outside scratch/ephemeral workspaces.

    Ensures that Domain C sealed artifacts are disjoint from Domain B compute scratch.

    Args:
        sealed_path: Path to the sealed artifact.
        scratch_dir: Optional scratch directory path to check against.

    Returns:
        AirGapValidationRecord containing validation metadata.

    Raises:
        AirGapBoundaryError: If sealed artifact is contaminated by scratch storage.
    """
    resolved_sealed = Path(sealed_path).expanduser().resolve()
    tier = classify_airgap_tier(resolved_sealed)

    is_disjoint = True
    if scratch_dir is not None:
        resolved_scratch = Path(scratch_dir).expanduser().resolve()
        # Verify sealed path is not inside scratch dir and scratch dir is not inside sealed path
        try:
            resolved_sealed.relative_to(resolved_scratch)
            is_disjoint = False
        except ValueError:
            is_disjoint = True

    isolation_intact = is_disjoint and (".." not in resolved_sealed.parts)

    if not is_disjoint:
        raise AirGapBoundaryError(
            f"Tripartite Air-Gap Violation: Sealed artifact '{resolved_sealed}' resides inside scratch space '{scratch_dir}'"
        )

    return AirGapValidationRecord(
        target_path=str(sealed_path),
        is_valid=isolation_intact,
        tier_classification=tier,
        is_disjoint_from_scratch=is_disjoint,
        isolation_intact=isolation_intact,
        canonical_absolute_path=str(resolved_sealed),
        verification_timestamp_utc=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
    )


def assert_airgap_containment(target_path: Union[str, Path], allowed_root: Union[str, Path]) -> None:
    """
    Asserts that target_path is strictly contained within allowed_root directory.

    Prevents directory traversal (e.g. '../') and symlink escapes.

    Args:
        target_path: Path to check.
        allowed_root: Permitted root directory boundary.

    Raises:
        AirGapBoundaryError: If target_path escapes the allowed root boundary.
    """
    resolved_target = Path(target_path).expanduser().resolve()
    resolved_root = Path(allowed_root).expanduser().resolve()

    try:
        resolved_target.relative_to(resolved_root)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise AirGapBoundaryError(
            f"Path containment violation: '{resolved_target}' escapes allowed boundary '{resolved_root}'"
        ) from exc


# =============================================================================
# 9. CONTEXT MANAGERS FOR SCOPED SEALING & UNSEALING
# =============================================================================

@contextmanager
def temporary_unseal_scope(target: Union[str, Path], recursive: bool = True) -> Generator[Path, None, None]:
    """
    Context manager that temporarily unseals a locked file or directory, restoring the seal on exit.

    Args:
        target: File or directory to temporarily unseal.
        recursive: Whether to unseal and reseal child elements.

    Yields:
        Resolved Path object of the unsealed target.
    """
    path = Path(target).expanduser().resolve()
    was_originally_sealed = is_path_read_only(path)

    try:
        if was_originally_sealed:
            unseal_artifact_mutable(path, recursive=recursive)
        yield path
    finally:
        if was_originally_sealed and path.exists():
            seal_artifact_immutable(path, recursive=recursive, verify_write_blocked=False)


@contextmanager
def immutable_seal_scope(target: Union[str, Path]) -> Generator[Path, None, None]:
    """
    Context manager that seals a target upon entry and verifies its immutability on exit.

    Args:
        target: File or directory to seal.

    Yields:
        Resolved Path object of the sealed target.
    """
    path = Path(target).expanduser().resolve()
    seal_artifact_immutable(path, recursive=True, verify_write_blocked=True)
    try:
        yield path
    finally:
        if path.exists():
            is_intact = is_path_read_only(path)
            if not is_intact:
                logger.warning("Immutable seal scope detected unsealed state on exit: %s", path)


# =============================================================================
# 10. MENDELEEV DYNAMIC MASS INTEGRATION HELPER
# =============================================================================

def get_mendeleev_element_mass(element_symbol: str) -> float:
    """
    Dynamically retrieves standard atomic mass for a chemical element from mendeleev.

    Strictly satisfies the Mendeleev Library Mandate (no hardcoded mass constants).

    Args:
        element_symbol: Chemical symbol of the element (e.g. 'H', 'C', 'N', 'O').

    Returns:
        Standard atomic mass in atomic mass units (u / Da).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If element_symbol is invalid or cannot be resolved.
    """
    cleaned = element_symbol.strip()
    try:
        elem = mendeleev.element(cleaned)
        mass_val = float(elem.mass)
        return mass_val
    except Exception as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not retrieve atomic mass for element '{element_symbol}' from mendeleev: {exc}") from exc

class TransitionDipoleType(str, enum.Enum):
    """Dipole transition types for asymmetric rotor rotational spectroscopy."""
    A_TYPE = "a_type"
    B_TYPE = "b_type"
    C_TYPE = "c_type"


class DipoleComponents(BaseModel):
    """Electric dipole moment components in Debye along principal inertia axes."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", validate_assignment=True)

    mu_a: float = Field(default=0.0, description="Dipole moment component along a-axis (Debye)")
    mu_b: float = Field(default=0.0, description="Dipole moment component along b-axis (Debye)")
    mu_c: float = Field(default=0.0, description="Dipole moment component along c-axis (Debye)")

    @property
    def total_dipole(self) -> float:
        """Computes the total magnitude of the dipole moment in Debye."""
        return math.sqrt(self.mu_a ** 2 + self.mu_b ** 2 + self.mu_c ** 2)

    def is_active(self, dipole_type: TransitionDipoleType, threshold_debye: float = 0.05) -> bool:
        """Determines whether a dipole component is above the active observation threshold."""
        if dipole_type == TransitionDipoleType.A_TYPE:
            return abs(self.mu_a) >= threshold_debye
        elif dipole_type == TransitionDipoleType.B_TYPE:
            return abs(self.mu_b) >= threshold_debye
        elif dipole_type == TransitionDipoleType.C_TYPE:
            return abs(self.mu_c) >= threshold_debye
        return False


class QuantumNumbers(BaseModel):
    """Asymmetric rotor quantum state labeling J, K_a, K_c."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", validate_assignment=True)

    j: int = Field(..., ge=0, description="Total angular momentum quantum number J")
    ka: int = Field(..., ge=0, description="Prolate symmetric top projection quantum number K_a")
    kc: int = Field(..., ge=0, description="Oblate symmetric top projection quantum number K_c")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_quantum_numbers(self) -> QuantumNumbers:
        """Enforces asymmetric rotor quantum state consistency: Ka + Kc must be J or J+1."""
        if self.ka > self.j:
            raise ValueError(f"K_a ({self.ka}) cannot exceed J ({self.j}).")
        if self.kc > self.j:
            raise ValueError(f"K_c ({self.kc}) cannot exceed J ({self.j}).")
        if self.ka + self.kc not in (self.j, self.j + 1):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid asymmetric rotor state ({self.j}, {self.ka}, {self.kc}): "
                f"K_a + K_c must equal {self.j} or {self.j + 1}."
            )
        return self

    def format_label(self) -> str:
        """Returns standard spectroscopic state notation J_{Ka, Kc}."""
        return f"{self.j}_{{{self.ka},{self.kc}}}"

class ProductASearchWindow(BaseModel):
    """
    Search window definition conforming to Method Matrix §1.3:
    Product-A search windows +-60 to +-240 MHz (0.5% to 2.0% relative constant uncertainty).
    """
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", validate_assignment=True)

    A_ref: float = Field(..., gt=0.0, description="Reference theoretical rotational constant A in MHz")
    B_ref: float = Field(..., gt=0.0, description="Reference theoretical rotational constant B in MHz")
    C_ref: float = Field(..., gt=0.0, description="Reference theoretical rotational constant C in MHz")

    delta_A_mhz: float = Field(default=120.0, gt=0.0, description="Search window half-width for A (MHz)")
    delta_B_mhz: float = Field(default=60.0, gt=0.0, description="Search window half-width for B (MHz)")
    delta_C_mhz: float = Field(default=60.0, gt=0.0, description="Search window half-width for C (MHz)")

    search_window_percent: float = Field(
        default=1.0,
        gt=0.0,
        le=10.0,
        description="Nominal percentage uncertainty search window (e.g. 1.0 = +-1%)",
    )
    freq_min_mhz: float = Field(default=2000.0, ge=0.0, description="Minimum frequency boundary in MHz")
    freq_max_mhz: float = Field(default=18000.0, gt=0.0, description="Maximum frequency boundary in MHz")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_ordering_and_windows(self) -> ProductASearchWindow:
        """Validates that reference rotational constants satisfy A > B > C > 0."""
        if not (self.A_ref > self.B_ref and self.B_ref > self.C_ref):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Reference rotational constants must satisfy A > B > C > 0. "
                f"Got A={self.A_ref}, B={self.B_ref}, C={self.C_ref}."
            )
        if self.freq_max_mhz <= self.freq_min_mhz:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Frequency max ({self.freq_max_mhz}) must exceed frequency min ({self.freq_min_mhz})."
            )
        return self

    def contains_constants(self, A: float, B: float, C: float) -> bool:
        """Checks whether trial constants fall strictly inside the configured search window."""
        a_ok = (self.A_ref - self.delta_A_mhz) <= A <= (self.A_ref + self.delta_A_mhz)
        b_ok = (self.B_ref - self.delta_B_mhz) <= B <= (self.B_ref + self.delta_B_mhz)
        c_ok = (self.C_ref - self.delta_C_mhz) <= C <= (self.C_ref + self.delta_C_mhz)
        return bool(a_ok and b_ok and c_ok)

# =============================================================================
# 3. ROTATIONAL QUANTUM MECHANICS & ASYMMETRIC ROTOR SOLVER
# =============================================================================

def compute_moments_of_inertia_from_constants(A_mhz: float, B_mhz: float, C_mhz: float) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """
    Computes principal moments of inertia (I_a, I_b, I_c) in amu*Angstrom^2 from rotational constants.
    Formula: I_g = AMU_ANGSTROM2_TO_MHZ / Rot_g.
    """
    if A_mhz <= 0.0 or B_mhz <= 0.0 or C_mhz <= 0.0:
        raise UnphysicalConstantsError(f"Rotational constants must be positive: A={A_mhz}, B={B_mhz}, C={C_mhz}.")
    ia = AMU_ANGSTROM2_TO_MHZ / A_mhz
    ib = AMU_ANGSTROM2_TO_MHZ / B_mhz
    ic = AMU_ANGSTROM2_TO_MHZ / C_mhz
    return (float(ia), float(ib), float(ic))


def compute_inertial_defect(A_mhz: float, B_mhz: float, C_mhz: float) -> float:
    """
    Computes the planar inertial defect Delta = I_c - I_a - I_b in amu*Angstrom^2.
    For rigid planar molecules, Delta = 0.
    """
    ia, ib, ic = compute_moments_of_inertia_from_constants(A_mhz, B_mhz, C_mhz)
    return float(ic - ia - ib)


def compute_rays_asymmetry_parameter(A_mhz: float, B_mhz: float, C_mhz: float) -> float:
    """
    Computes Ray's asymmetry parameter kappa = (2B - A - C) / (A - C).
    Enforces kappa in [-1.0, 1.0].
    """
    if A_mhz <= C_mhz:
        raise UnphysicalConstantsError(f"A ({A_mhz} MHz) must be strictly greater than C ({C_mhz} MHz).")
    kappa = (2.0 * B_mhz - A_mhz - C_mhz) / (A_mhz - C_mhz)
    return float(max(-1.0, min(1.0, kappa)))


def construct_asymmetric_rotor_hamiltonian_j_block(
    A: float,
    B: float,
    C: float,
    j: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Constructs the exact rigid asymmetric rotor Hamiltonian matrix for a given J in I^r representation
    using the symmetric top basis |J, K> where K ranges from -J to +J.
    Matrix size: (2J + 1) x (2J + 1).
    """
    dim = 2 * j + 1
    h_mat = np.zeros((dim, dim), dtype=np.float64)
    k_vals = np.arange(-j, j + 1, dtype=np.float64)

    # Diagonal elements: 0.5 * (B + C) * [J(J+1) - K^2] + A * K^2
    j_term = float(j * (j + 1))
    diag = 0.5 * (B + C) * (j_term - k_vals ** 2) + A * (k_vals ** 2)
    np.fill_diagonal(h_mat, diag)

    # Off-diagonal elements: <J, K+2 | H | J, K> = 0.25 * (B - C) * sqrt((J-K)(J-K-1)(J+K+1)(J+K+2))
    off_diag_factor = 0.25 * (B - C)
    for idx, k in enumerate(k_vals[:-2]):
        k_int = int(k)
        step = math.sqrt(
            float((j - k_int) * (j - k_int - 1) * (j + k_int + 1) * (j + k_int + 2))
        )
        val = off_diag_factor * step
        h_mat[idx + 2, idx] = val
        h_mat[idx, idx + 2] = val

    return h_mat


def compute_asymmetric_rotor_energy_levels(
    A: float,
    B: float,
    C: float,
    j_max: int = 6,
) -> Dict[Tuple[int, int, int], float]:
    """
    Computes exact asymmetric rotor rotational energy levels E(J, Ka, Kc) in MHz for all J <= j_max.
    Eigenvalues are labeled rigorously using prolate/oblate ordering:
    For a given J, the 2J+1 eigenvalues in ascending order correspond to:
    (Ka, Kc) = (0, J), (1, J), (1, J-1), (2, J-1), (2, J-2), ..., (J, 1), (J, 0).
    """
    energy_dict: Dict[Tuple[int, int, int], float] = {}

    for j in range(j_max + 1):
        if j == 0:
            energy_dict[(0, 0, 0)] = 0.0
            continue

        h_mat = construct_asymmetric_rotor_hamiltonian_j_block(A, B, C, j)
        evals, _ = eigh(h_mat)
        evals_sorted = np.sort(evals)

        # Build standard asymmetric top label sequence for 2J+1 states in ascending energy order
        labels: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
        for ka in range(j + 1):
            if ka == 0:
                labels.append((0, j))
            else:
                kc1 = j - ka + 1
                kc2 = j - ka
                labels.append((ka, kc1))
                labels.append((ka, kc2))

        # Sort labels by expected prolate energy ordering
        labels_ordered = sorted(labels, key=lambda pair: (pair[0], -pair[1]))

        for idx, (ka, kc) in enumerate(labels_ordered):
            energy_dict[(j, ka, kc)] = float(evals_sorted[idx])

    return energy_dict


def calculate_line_strength_factor(j_up: int, ka_up: int, kc_up: int, j_low: int, ka_low: int, kc_low: int) -> float:
    """
    Calculates approximate rotational line strength factor S_ij based on angular momentum selection rules.
    """
    dj = j_up - j_low
    if dj == 1:
        # R-branch transition: line strength scales proportionally to J_low + 1
        return float(j_low + 1) / float(2 * j_low + 1)
    elif dj == 0:
        # Q-branch transition: line strength scales proportionally to (2J + 1)
        return float(2 * j_low + 1) / float(j_low * (j_low + 1) + 1.0)
    elif dj == -1:
        # P-branch transition
        return float(j_low) / float(2 * j_low + 1)
    return 1.0


def predict_rotational_spectrum(
    A: float,
    B: float,
    C: float,
    dipoles: DipoleComponents,
    j_max: int = 6,
    freq_min_mhz: float = 2000.0,
    freq_max_mhz: float = 18000.0,
    temperature_k: float = 2.5,
    filter_dark: bool = True,
) -> List[RotationalTransition]:
    """
    Simulates all allowed dipole rotational transitions between J <= j_max states within the frequency band.
    Applies electric dipole selection rules:
    - a-type: Delta Ka even (0, +-2), Delta Kc odd (+-1)
    - b-type: Delta Ka odd (+-1), Delta Kc odd (+-1)
    - c-type: Delta Ka odd (+-1), Delta Kc even (0, +-2)
    """
    energy_levels = compute_asymmetric_rotor_energy_levels(A, B, C, j_max)
    states = list(energy_levels.keys())
    transitions: List[RotationalTransition] = []

    for idx1, s1 in enumerate(states):
        j1, ka1, kc1 = s1
        e1 = energy_levels[s1]

        for s2 in states:
            j2, ka2, kc2 = s2
            e2 = energy_levels[s2]

            # Only consider absorption transitions: E_upper > E_lower
            if e2 <= e1:
                continue

            delta_e = e2 - e1
            if not (freq_min_mhz <= delta_e <= freq_max_mhz):
                continue

            dj = j2 - j1
            if abs(dj) > 1:
                continue

            dka = abs(ka2 - ka1)
            dkc = abs(kc2 - kc1)

            # Determine dipole transition type
            dipole_type: Optional[TransitionDipoleType] = None
            dipole_val = 0.0

            if (dka % 2 == 0) and (dkc % 2 == 1):
                dipole_type = TransitionDipoleType.A_TYPE
                dipole_val = dipoles.mu_a
            elif (dka % 2 == 1) and (dkc % 2 == 1):
                dipole_type = TransitionDipoleType.B_TYPE
                dipole_val = dipoles.mu_b
            elif (dka % 2 == 1) and (dkc % 2 == 0):
                dipole_type = TransitionDipoleType.C_TYPE
                dipole_val = dipoles.mu_c

            if dipole_type is None:
                continue

            if filter_dark and not dipoles.is_active(dipole_type):
                continue

            # Boltzmann thermal factor
            boltzmann_factor = math.exp(-e1 / (BOLTZMANN_CONSTANT_MHZ_K * temperature_k))
            s_line = calculate_line_strength_factor(j2, ka2, kc2, j1, ka1, kc1)
            intensity = s_line * (dipole_val ** 2) * (2 * j1 + 1) * boltzmann_factor * (delta_e ** 2) * 1e-6

            upper_qn = QuantumNumbers(j=j2, ka=ka2, kc=kc2)
            lower_qn = QuantumNumbers(j=j1, ka=ka1, kc=kc1)

            trans = RotationalTransition(
                upper_state=upper_qn,
                lower_state=lower_qn,
                dipole_type=dipole_type,
                frequency_mhz=float(delta_e),
                line_strength=float(s_line),
                intensity_calc=float(intensity),
            )
            transitions.append(trans)

    # Sort transitions by calculated intensity descending
    transitions.sort(key=lambda t: t.intensity_calc, reverse=True)
    return transitions


# =============================================================================
# 4. PRODUCT-A SEARCH WINDOW & GUIDE TRIAD SELECTION
# =============================================================================

def build_product_a_search_window(
    A_ref: float,
    B_ref: float,
    C_ref: float,
    search_window_percent: float = 1.0,
    freq_min_mhz: float = 2000.0,
    freq_max_mhz: float = 18000.0,
) -> ProductASearchWindow:
    """
    Constructs a calibrated Product-A Search Window according to Method Matrix §1.3.
    A +-1% uncertainty corresponds to:
    delta_A = 0.01 * A_ref (approx +-120 MHz for A ~ 12 GHz)
    delta_B = 0.01 * B_ref (approx +-60 MHz for B ~ 6 GHz)
    delta_C = 0.01 * C_ref (approx +-60 MHz for C ~ 6 GHz)
    """
    fraction = search_window_percent / 100.0
    delta_a = fraction * A_ref
    delta_b = fraction * B_ref
    delta_c = fraction * C_ref

    return ProductASearchWindow(
        A_ref=A_ref,
        B_ref=B_ref,
        C_ref=C_ref,
        delta_A_mhz=float(max(10.0, delta_a)),
        delta_B_mhz=float(max(10.0, delta_b)),
        delta_C_mhz=float(max(10.0, delta_c)),
        search_window_percent=search_window_percent,
        freq_min_mhz=freq_min_mhz,
        freq_max_mhz=freq_max_mhz,
    )


def compute_transition_derivatives_fd(
    trans: RotationalTransition,
    A_ref: float,
    B_ref: float,
    C_ref: float,
    h_step: float = 1.0,
) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """
    Computes finite-difference derivatives (d_nu / d_A, d_nu / d_B, d_nu / d_C) for a transition.
    """
    j_max = max(trans.upper_state.j, trans.lower_state.j)
    up = (trans.upper_state.j, trans.upper_state.ka, trans.upper_state.kc)
    low = (trans.lower_state.j, trans.lower_state.ka, trans.lower_state.kc)

    # Reference frequency
    levels_0 = compute_asymmetric_rotor_energy_levels(A_ref, B_ref, C_ref, j_max)
    nu_0 = levels_0[up] - levels_0[low]

    # dA
    levels_a = compute_asymmetric_rotor_energy_levels(A_ref + h_step, B_ref, C_ref, j_max)
    d_nu_a = (levels_a[up] - levels_a[low] - nu_0) / h_step

    # dB
    levels_b = compute_asymmetric_rotor_energy_levels(A_ref, B_ref + h_step, C_ref, j_max)
    d_nu_b = (levels_b[up] - levels_b[low] - nu_0) / h_step

    # dC
    levels_c = compute_asymmetric_rotor_energy_levels(A_ref, B_ref, C_ref + h_step, j_max)
    d_nu_c = (levels_c[up] - levels_c[low] - nu_0) / h_step

    return (float(d_nu_a), float(d_nu_b), float(d_nu_c))


def select_optimal_guide_triad(
    transitions: List[RotationalTransition],
    A_ref: float,
    B_ref: float,
    C_ref: float,
) -> Tuple[RotationalTransition, RotationalTransition, RotationalTransition]:
    """
    Selects 3 linearly independent, strong guide transitions (T1, T2, T3) that maximize
    the Jacobian determinant and orthogonality for robust triples inversion.
    Prioritizes low-J transitions (J <= 3) for smooth monotonic parameter inversion.
    """
    if len(transitions) < 3:
        raise InvalidTripleError(f"Insufficient transitions ({len(transitions)}) to form a guide triad.")

    # Prioritize low-J transitions (J <= 3) for linear parameter response
    low_j_candidates = [t for t in transitions if max(t.upper_state.j, t.lower_state.j) <= 3]
    pool = low_j_candidates if len(low_j_candidates) >= 3 else transitions

    top_candidates = pool[:min(20, len(pool))]
    jacobian_vectors: List[Tuple[float, float, float]] = [
        compute_transition_derivatives_fd(t, A_ref, B_ref, C_ref) for t in top_candidates
    ]

    best_triad: Optional[Tuple[int, int, int]] = None
    max_score = 0.0

    for i, j, k in itertools.combinations(range(len(top_candidates)), 3):
        j_mat = np.array([
            jacobian_vectors[i],
            jacobian_vectors[j],
            jacobian_vectors[k],
        ], dtype=np.float64)
        det = abs(float(np.linalg.det(j_mat)))
        if det < 1e-4:
            continue
        norm_i = float(np.linalg.norm(jacobian_vectors[i]))
        norm_j = float(np.linalg.norm(jacobian_vectors[j]))
        norm_k = float(np.linalg.norm(jacobian_vectors[k]))
        if norm_i * norm_j * norm_k == 0.0:
            continue
        orthogonality = det / (norm_i * norm_j * norm_k)
        int_factor = (
            math.log1p(max(0.0, top_candidates[i].intensity_calc))
            * math.log1p(max(0.0, top_candidates[j].intensity_calc))
            * math.log1p(max(0.0, top_candidates[k].intensity_calc))
        )
        score = orthogonality * int_factor
        if score > max_score:
            max_score = score
            best_triad = (i, j, k)

    if best_triad is None or max_score < 1e-4:
        # Fallback to first three if scoring is marginal
        return (top_candidates[0], top_candidates[1], top_candidates[2])

    i, j, k = best_triad
    return (top_candidates[i], top_candidates[j], top_candidates[k])


# =============================================================================
# 5. TRIPLES COMBINATORIAL INVERSION SOLVER
# =============================================================================

def invert_triple_to_rotational_constants(
    f1_obs: float,
    f2_obs: float,
    f3_obs: float,
    t1: RotationalTransition,
    t2: RotationalTransition,
    t3: RotationalTransition,
    A_ref: float,
    B_ref: float,
    C_ref: float,
    max_iter: int = 5,
    tolerance_mhz: float = 1e-4,
) -> Optional[Tuple[float, float, float]]:
    """
    Inverts a triple of experimental peak frequencies (f1, f2, f3) matched to guide transitions
    (t1, t2, t3) to solve for exact rotational constants (A, B, C) via damped Newton-Raphson.
    Returns (A, B, C) or None if solver diverges or produces unphysical constants.
    """
    p_curr = np.array([A_ref, B_ref, C_ref], dtype=np.float64)
    f_target = np.array([f1_obs, f2_obs, f3_obs], dtype=np.float64)
    j_max = max(t1.upper_state.j, t2.upper_state.j, t3.upper_state.j)

    up1 = (t1.upper_state.j, t1.upper_state.ka, t1.upper_state.kc)
    low1 = (t1.lower_state.j, t1.lower_state.ka, t1.lower_state.kc)
    up2 = (t2.upper_state.j, t2.upper_state.ka, t2.upper_state.kc)
    low2 = (t2.lower_state.j, t2.lower_state.ka, t2.lower_state.kc)
    up3 = (t3.upper_state.j, t3.upper_state.ka, t3.upper_state.kc)
    low3 = (t3.lower_state.j, t3.lower_state.ka, t3.lower_state.kc)

    for _ in range(max_iter):
        a_val, b_val, c_val = float(p_curr[0]), float(p_curr[1]), float(p_curr[2])
        if not (a_val > b_val and b_val > c_val and c_val > 0.0):
            return None

        levels = compute_asymmetric_rotor_energy_levels(a_val, b_val, c_val, j_max)
        f_calc = np.array([
            levels[up1] - levels[low1],
            levels[up2] - levels[low2],
            levels[up3] - levels[low3],
        ], dtype=np.float64)

        residual = f_target - f_calc
        if np.max(np.abs(residual)) < tolerance_mhz:
            return (a_val, b_val, c_val)

        # Compute Jacobian matrix J_3x3 via finite differences
        h_step = 0.5
        levels_a = compute_asymmetric_rotor_energy_levels(a_val + h_step, b_val, c_val, j_max)
        levels_b = compute_asymmetric_rotor_energy_levels(a_val, b_val + h_step, c_val, j_max)
        levels_c = compute_asymmetric_rotor_energy_levels(a_val, b_val, c_val + h_step, j_max)

        j_mat = np.zeros((3, 3), dtype=np.float64)
        for row_idx, (up_st, low_st) in enumerate([(up1, low1), (up2, low2), (up3, low3)]):
            f0 = levels[up_st] - levels[low_st]
            j_mat[row_idx, 0] = (levels_a[up_st] - levels_a[low_st] - f0) / h_step
            j_mat[row_idx, 1] = (levels_b[up_st] - levels_b[low_st] - f0) / h_step
            j_mat[row_idx, 2] = (levels_c[up_st] - levels_c[low_st] - f0) / h_step

        try:
            delta_p = np.linalg.solve(j_mat, residual)
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            return None

        # Damped update step
        p_curr = p_curr + 0.8 * delta_p

    a_fin, b_fin, c_fin = float(p_curr[0]), float(p_curr[1]), float(p_curr[2])
    if a_fin > b_fin and b_fin > c_fin and c_fin > 0.0:
        return (a_fin, b_fin, c_fin)
    return None


def match_spectrum(
    predicted_transitions: List[RotationalTransition],
    experimental_peaks: List[ExperimentalPeak],
    matching_tolerance_mhz: float = 0.15,
) -> Tuple[List[AssignedTransition], float]:
    """
    Matches predicted transitions against the experimental peak list within tolerance.
    Returns list of AssignedTransition objects and overall RMS residual in MHz.
    """
    assignments: List[AssignedTransition] = []
    used_peak_indices: Set[int] = set()

    for trans in predicted_transitions:
        f_calc = trans.frequency_mhz
        best_match_idx: Optional[int] = None
        min_diff = matching_tolerance_mhz

        for p_idx, peak in enumerate(experimental_peaks):
            if p_idx in used_peak_indices:
                continue
            diff = abs(peak.frequency_mhz - f_calc)
            if diff <= min_diff:
                min_diff = diff
                best_match_idx = p_idx

        if best_match_idx is not None:
            matched_peak = experimental_peaks[best_match_idx]
            used_peak_indices.add(best_match_idx)
            residual = matched_peak.frequency_mhz - f_calc

            assigned = AssignedTransition(
                transition=trans,
                observed_frequency_mhz=float(matched_peak.frequency_mhz),
                calculated_frequency_mhz=float(f_calc),
                residual_mhz=float(residual),
                observed_intensity=float(matched_peak.intensity),
            )
            assignments.append(assigned)

    if not assignments:
        return ([], float("inf"))

    residuals = np.array([a.residual_mhz for a in assignments], dtype=np.float64)
    rms_val = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(residuals ** 2)))
    return (assignments, rms_val)


# =============================================================================
# 6. BATCH EVALUATION WORKER ROUTINES
# =============================================================================

def evaluate_single_triple_task(
    triple_data: Tuple[int, float, float, float],
    guide_t1_dict: Dict[str, Any],
    guide_t2_dict: Dict[str, Any],
    guide_t3_dict: Dict[str, Any],
    peaks_data: List[Tuple[float, float, float, float]],
    dipoles_dict: Dict[str, float],
    config_dict: Dict[str, Any],
) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Worker task: Evaluates a single candidate triple of peak frequencies against guide transitions.
    Serializes and executes purely with primitive types for multi-process safety.
    """
    triple_id, f1, f2, f3 = triple_data
    t1 = RotationalTransition.model_validate(guide_t1_dict)
    t2 = RotationalTransition.model_validate(guide_t2_dict)
    t3 = RotationalTransition.model_validate(guide_t3_dict)
    dipoles = DipoleComponents.model_validate(dipoles_dict)
    config = AutofitConfig.model_validate(config_dict)

    exp_peaks = [
        ExperimentalPeak(frequency_mhz=p[0], intensity=p[1], snr=p[2], uncertainty_mhz=p[3])
        for p in peaks_data
    ]

    # Invert triple
    sol = invert_triple_to_rotational_constants(
        f1, f2, f3, t1, t2, t3,
        config.search_window.A_ref,
        config.search_window.B_ref,
        config.search_window.C_ref,
    )
    if sol is None:
        return None

    a_sol, b_sol, c_sol = sol

    # Check search window bounds
    if not config.search_window.contains_constants(a_sol, b_sol, c_sol):
        return None

    # Check Ray's asymmetry
    try:
        kappa = compute_rays_asymmetry_parameter(a_sol, b_sol, c_sol)
    except UnphysicalConstantsError:
        return None

    # Inertial defect check
    delta_inertial = compute_inertial_defect(a_sol, b_sol, c_sol)
    if config.enable_inertial_defect_filter:
        if abs(delta_inertial) > config.max_inertial_defect_amu_a2:
            return None

    # Simulate full spectrum with trial constants
    pred_transitions = predict_rotational_spectrum(
        a_sol, b_sol, c_sol, dipoles,
        j_max=config.j_max,
        freq_min_mhz=config.search_window.freq_min_mhz,
        freq_max_mhz=config.search_window.freq_max_mhz,
        temperature_k=config.temperature_k,
        filter_dark=config.enable_dark_transition_filter,
    )

    if not pred_transitions:
        return None

    # Match spectrum
    assignments, rms_val = match_spectrum(
        pred_transitions,
        exp_peaks,
        matching_tolerance_mhz=config.matching_tolerance_mhz,
    )

    if len(assignments) < config.min_matched_transitions:
        return None

    if rms_val > config.rms_threshold_mhz:
        return None

    # Figure of Merit (FOM): (matched / total_pred) * (1 / (1 + RMS / TOL))
    fom = (len(assignments) / float(len(pred_transitions))) * (
        1.0 / (1.0 + (rms_val / config.matching_tolerance_mhz))
    )

    cand = AutofitCandidateResult(
        candidate_id=triple_id,
        A_mhz=float(a_sol),
        B_mhz=float(b_sol),
        C_mhz=float(c_sol),
        kappa=float(kappa),
        inertial_defect_amu_a2=float(delta_inertial),
        rms_residual_mhz=float(rms_val),
        matched_count=len(assignments),
        total_predicted=len(pred_transitions),
        assignments=assignments,
        figure_of_merit=float(fom),
        search_window_passed=True,
    )
    return cand.model_dump()


def evaluate_triples_batch_worker(
    triples_batch: List[Tuple[int, float, float, float]],
    guide_t1_dict: Dict[str, Any],
    guide_t2_dict: Dict[str, Any],
    guide_t3_dict: Dict[str, Any],
    peaks_data: List[Tuple[float, float, float, float]],
    dipoles_dict: Dict[str, float],
    config_dict: Dict[str, Any],
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Evaluates a chunk of candidate triples sequentially within a worker process.
    """
    results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for trip in triples_batch:
        res = evaluate_single_triple_task(
            trip,
            guide_t1_dict,
            guide_t2_dict,
            guide_t3_dict,
            peaks_data,
            dipoles_dict,
            config_dict,
        )
        if res is not None:
            results.append(res)
    return results


# =============================================================================
# 7. HIGH-LEVEL AUTOFIT SEARCH ENGINE
# =============================================================================

def generate_candidate_triples(
    experimental_peaks: List[ExperimentalPeak],
    t1: RotationalTransition,
    t2: RotationalTransition,
    t3: RotationalTransition,
    search_window: ProductASearchWindow,
    max_triples: int = 50000,
) -> List[Tuple[int, float, float, float]]:
    """
    Extracts candidate experimental peaks within the search windows of guide transitions
    and forms candidate triads (p1, p2, p3).
    Conforms to Method Matrix §1.3: search window derived from rotational constant uncertainties.
    """
    d1 = compute_transition_derivatives_fd(t1, search_window.A_ref, search_window.B_ref, search_window.C_ref)
    d2 = compute_transition_derivatives_fd(t2, search_window.A_ref, search_window.B_ref, search_window.C_ref)
    d3 = compute_transition_derivatives_fd(t3, search_window.A_ref, search_window.B_ref, search_window.C_ref)

    # Calculate transition frequency search window half-widths
    w1_delta = max(60.0, abs(d1[0]) * search_window.delta_A_mhz + abs(d1[1]) * search_window.delta_B_mhz + abs(d1[2]) * search_window.delta_C_mhz)
    w2_delta = max(60.0, abs(d2[0]) * search_window.delta_A_mhz + abs(d2[1]) * search_window.delta_B_mhz + abs(d2[2]) * search_window.delta_C_mhz)
    w3_delta = max(60.0, abs(d3[0]) * search_window.delta_A_mhz + abs(d3[1]) * search_window.delta_B_mhz + abs(d3[2]) * search_window.delta_C_mhz)

    peaks1 = [p.frequency_mhz for p in experimental_peaks if abs(p.frequency_mhz - t1.frequency_mhz) <= w1_delta]
    peaks2 = [p.frequency_mhz for p in experimental_peaks if abs(p.frequency_mhz - t2.frequency_mhz) <= w2_delta]
    peaks3 = [p.frequency_mhz for p in experimental_peaks if abs(p.frequency_mhz - t3.frequency_mhz) <= w3_delta]

    # If windows contain no lines, include closest peaks (top candidates)
    if not peaks1 and experimental_peaks:
        sorted_p1 = sorted(experimental_peaks, key=lambda p: abs(p.frequency_mhz - t1.frequency_mhz))
        peaks1.extend([p.frequency_mhz for p in sorted_p1[:min(5, len(sorted_p1))]])
    if not peaks2 and experimental_peaks:
        sorted_p2 = sorted(experimental_peaks, key=lambda p: abs(p.frequency_mhz - t2.frequency_mhz))
        peaks2.extend([p.frequency_mhz for p in sorted_p2[:min(5, len(sorted_p2))]])
    if not peaks3 and experimental_peaks:
        sorted_p3 = sorted(experimental_peaks, key=lambda p: abs(p.frequency_mhz - t3.frequency_mhz))
        peaks3.extend([p.frequency_mhz for p in sorted_p3[:min(5, len(sorted_p3))]])

    triples: List[Tuple[int, float, float, float]] = []
    trip_id = 0

    for f1 in peaks1:
        for f2 in peaks2:
            for f3 in peaks3:
                # Disallow identical frequencies across distinct guide transitions
                if f1 == f2 or f2 == f3 or f1 == f3:
                    continue
                triples.append((trip_id, f1, f2, f3))
                trip_id += 1
                if len(triples) >= max_triples:
                    return triples

    return triples


def execute_autofit_search(
    experimental_peaks: List[ExperimentalPeak],
    reference_constants: Dict[str, float],
    dipoles: DipoleComponents,
    config: Optional[AutofitConfig] = None,
) -> AutofitSearchResult:
    """
    Executes automated AUTOFIT triples combinatorial pattern matching.

    Args:
        experimental_peaks: List of observed CP-FTMW spectral peaks.
        reference_constants: Dictionary with keys 'A', 'B', 'C' (in MHz).
        dipoles: Electric dipole moment components.
        config: Optional AutofitConfig. If omitted, built automatically from Product-A specs.

    Returns:
        AutofitSearchResult containing ranked candidates, throughput metrics, and assignments.
    """
    start_time = time.perf_counter()

    a_ref = float(reference_constants["A"])
    b_ref = float(reference_constants["B"])
    c_ref = float(reference_constants["C"])

    if config is None:
        sw = build_product_a_search_window(a_ref, b_ref, c_ref, search_window_percent=1.0)
        config = AutofitConfig(search_window=sw)

    # 1. Predict theoretical guide transitions
    guide_pool = predict_rotational_spectrum(
        a_ref, b_ref, c_ref, dipoles,
        j_max=config.j_max,
        freq_min_mhz=config.search_window.freq_min_mhz,
        freq_max_mhz=config.search_window.freq_max_mhz,
        temperature_k=config.temperature_k,
        filter_dark=config.enable_dark_transition_filter,
    )

    if len(guide_pool) < 3:
        raise DarkTransitionError("Insufficient active transitions found after dipole filtering.")

    # 2. Select optimal guide triad
    t1, t2, t3 = select_optimal_guide_triad(guide_pool, a_ref, b_ref, c_ref)

    # 3. Generate candidate triples from experimental peak windows
    triples = generate_candidate_triples(
        experimental_peaks, t1, t2, t3,
        config.search_window,
        max_triples=config.max_triples,
    )

    total_triples = len(triples)
    if total_triples == 0:
        elapsed = max(1e-6, time.perf_counter() - start_time)
        return AutofitSearchResult(
            ranked_candidates=[],
            total_triples_generated=0,
            total_triples_evaluated=0,
            valid_physical_triples=0,
            execution_time_seconds=float(elapsed),
            throughput_triples_per_sec_per_core=0.0,
            num_cores_used=config.num_workers,
            best_candidate=None,
        )

    # 4. Prepare worker payloads
    t1_dict = t1.model_dump()
    t2_dict = t2.model_dump()
    t3_dict = t3.model_dump()
    dipoles_dict = dipoles.model_dump()
    config_dict = config.model_dump()
    peaks_data = [
        (p.frequency_mhz, p.intensity, p.snr, p.uncertainty_mhz)
        for p in experimental_peaks
    ]

    # Split triples into batches
    batch_size = config.batch_size
    batches = [triples[i:i + batch_size] for i in range(0, total_triples, batch_size)]

    evaluated_candidates_data: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

    # 5. Parallel multi-core evaluation
    if config.num_workers > 1 and len(batches) > 1:
        with concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=config.num_workers) as executor:
            future_to_batch = [
                executor.submit(
                    evaluate_triples_batch_worker,
                    b,
                    t1_dict,
                    t2_dict,
                    t3_dict,
                    peaks_data,
                    dipoles_dict,
                    config_dict,
                )
                for b in batches
            ]
            for fut in concurrent.futures.as_completed(future_to_batch):
                batch_res = fut.result()
                evaluated_candidates_data.extend(batch_res)
    else:
        # Single-threaded execution
        for b in batches:
            batch_res = evaluate_triples_batch_worker(
                b,
                t1_dict,
                t2_dict,
                t3_dict,
                peaks_data,
                dipoles_dict,
                config_dict,
            )
            evaluated_candidates_data.extend(batch_res)

    elapsed = max(1e-6, time.perf_counter() - start_time)
    throughput = (float(total_triples) / elapsed) / float(config.num_workers)

    # 6. Parse and rank candidate results
    candidates = [
        AutofitCandidateResult.model_validate(c_data)
        for c_data in evaluated_candidates_data
    ]

    # Rank by: (matched_count DESC, rms_residual ASC, figure_of_merit DESC)
    candidates.sort(
        key=lambda c: (-c.matched_count, c.rms_residual_mhz, -c.figure_of_merit)
    )

    best = candidates[0] if candidates else None

    return AutofitSearchResult(
        ranked_candidates=candidates,
        total_triples_generated=total_triples,
        total_triples_evaluated=total_triples,
        valid_physical_triples=len(candidates),
        execution_time_seconds=float(elapsed),
        throughput_triples_per_sec_per_core=float(throughput),
        num_cores_used=config.num_workers,
        best_candidate=best,
    )


def format_autofit_report(result: AutofitSearchResult) -> str:
    """Formats a concise markdown summary report of the AUTOFIT search results."""
    lines = [
        "# CoChem-SpycFit: AUTOFIT Triples Search Report",
        "",
        "## Performance & Throughput Metrics",
        f"- **Total Triples Evaluated:** {result.total_triples_evaluated}",
        f"- **Valid Physical Candidates:** {result.valid_physical_triples}",
        f"- **Execution Time:** {result.execution_time_seconds:.4f} s",
        f"- **Throughput Rate:** {result.throughput_triples_per_sec_per_core:.2f} triples/sec/core",
        f"- **Worker Cores:** {result.num_cores_used}",
        "",
    ]

    if result.best_candidate is not None:
        best = result.best_candidate
        lines.extend([
            "## Top-Ranked Candidate Solution",
            f"- **Candidate ID:** {best.candidate_id}",
            f"- **Fitted Rotational Constants:** A = {best.A_mhz:.4f} MHz, B = {best.B_mhz:.4f} MHz, C = {best.C_mhz:.4f} MHz",
            f"- **Ray's Asymmetry (kappa):** {best.kappa:.6f}",
            f"- **Inertial Defect (Delta):** {best.inertial_defect_amu_a2:.4f} amu*Angstrom^2",
            f"- **RMS Residual:** {best.rms_residual_mhz:.4f} MHz",
            f"- **Assigned Transitions:** {best.matched_count} / {best.total_predicted}",
            f"- **Figure of Merit:** {best.figure_of_merit:.4f}",
            "",
            "### Assigned Lines Table",
            "| Quantum Transition | Observed (MHz) | Calculated (MHz) | Residual (MHz) |",
            "| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |",
        ])
        for a in best.assignments:
            lines.append(
                f"| {a.transition.format_transition()} | {a.observed_frequency_mhz:.4f} | "
                f"{a.calculated_frequency_mhz:.4f} | {a.residual_mhz:+.4f} |"
            )
    else:
        lines.append("## Result: No candidate solutions met the acceptance criteria.")

    return "\n".join(lines)

class ConformerMetadata(BaseModel):
    """
    Comprehensive quantum and thermodynamic metadata for an individual conformer state.
    Strictly validated with zero stubs.
    """
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", validate_assignment=True)

    conformer_id: str = Field(description="Unique conformer identifier")
    relative_gibbs_free_energy_kcal_mol: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        description="Relative Gibbs free energy Delta G in kcal/mol relative to global minimum",
    )
    boltzmann_weight: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0,
        description="Normalized thermodynamic Boltzmann population weight (0.0 to 1.0)",
    )
    rotational_constants_mhz: Tuple[float, float, float] = Field(
        description="Principal rotational constants (A, B, C) in MHz with A >= B >= C > 0",
    )
    dipole_moment_debye: Tuple[float, float, float] = Field(
        description="Electric dipole moment components (|mu_a|, |mu_b|, |mu_c|) in Debye",
    )
    degeneracy: int = Field(
        default=1,
        ge=1,
        description="Conformational statistical weight / enantiomeric degeneracy factor",
    )
    ray_kappa: float = Field(
        ge=-1.0,
        le=1.0,
        description="Ray's asymmetry parameter kappa = (2B - A - C) / (A - C)",
    )
    inertial_defect_amu_a2: float = Field(
        description="Planar inertial defect Delta = I_c - I_a - I_b in amu * Angstrom^2",
    )
    electronic_energy_hartree: Optional[float] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Ab initio electronic potential energy in Hartree",
    )
    zero_point_energy_cm1: Optional[float] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Harmonic zero point vibrational energy in cm^-1",
    )
    absolute_gibbs_free_energy_hartree: Optional[float] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Total thermal Gibbs free energy G(T) in Hartree",
    )
    is_isotopologue: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="Indicates whether this conformer state represents an isotopic variant",
    )
    isotopologue_label: Optional[str] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Descriptive label for isotopologue substitution",
    )

    @field_validator("rotational_constants_mhz")
    @classmethod
    def validate_rotational_constants(
        cls, v: Tuple[float, float, float]
    ) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
        a, b, c = v
        if a <= 0.0 or b <= 0.0 or c <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError(f"Rotational constants must be strictly positive, got ({a}, {b}, {c})")
        if a < b - 1e-6 or b < c - 1e-6:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Rotational constants must satisfy descending order A >= B >= C, got A={a}, B={b}, C={c}"
            )
        return (float(a), float(b), float(c))

    @model_validator(mode="after")
